notes: Deliverables were referencing features and vendors a customer's fleet doesn't actually have -- e.g. a customer with zero MetroCluster nodes had 'MetroCluster Issues' listed as a corrective action. Root cause: the enrichment KB matching engine scored articles as fleet-relevant from a title-text match against the fleet's ONTAP version/platform alone, never checking whether the customer's own systems have that feature. Added feature gates: MetroCluster/FabricPool/SnapMirror/ARP require confirmed presence on the customer's own systems; SnapLock, Zero Trust, MAV, Antivirus, Encryption, Audit, and every third-party vendor (Veeam, Commvault, VMware, Oracle, Cisco, Kubernetes/Trident, etc.) have no backing field in Active IQ's API at all, so none of them can earn fleet-specific relevance anymore. Also fixed a redundant IMT interoperability signal pass that leaked one customer's vendor evidence into another's findings, a dormant bug rendering literal 'NVE: undefined%' and fabricating NVE/Audit/SnapLock/MAV as top gaps in every deliverable, and unreliable MetroCluster/StorageGRID detection that could miss real systems.
